correctness.rationale: The polytope has exactly 24 signed-permutation vertices of (1,t,0) for 1<c<2 and (1,1,u) for 2<c<3; degeneracies at c=1,2,3 are limits of valid vertices. The signed four-point tetrahedron determinant is separately affine in its vertices, so its absolute maximum occurs on vertex quadruples. Independently reconstructed all 10,626 quadruples per branch as exact affine-coordinate polynomials (109 distinct in the lower branch, 97 in the upper) and verified all degree-three rational Bernstein coefficients of each E±p on [0,1/2],[1/2,1],[0,1] nonnegative, with actual matching determinant polynomials. This proves a CONTINUOUS all-parameter bound, not finite parameter sampling. Direct cap subtraction gives Vol(K_c)=4/3(1+3t+3t²−2t³) for c≤2, and 4/3[6−(1−u)^3] for c≥2. Independently verified factorizations 6(1+t+2t²)−4F=2(t+1)(2t−1)^2, 6t−F=(2t−1)(t²−t+1), and derivative sign for last ratio as −(u^4−16u+3)/(u³−3u²+3u+5)^2. Together prove unique global 1/6 minimum at c=3/2, second higher local minimum at unique u∈(0,1) solving u^4−16u+3=0, and witnesses in source. Checker source inspected but independent certificate computation implemented in independent_checks.py, not trust in saved VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: Maximal simplices of a polytope are a standard, nontrivial affine extremal invariant. The K_c family connects two classical symmetric polytopes with combinatorial changes, and the exact three regimes, exceptional global minimizing truncated octahedron at c=3/2, and secondary local minimum resolve a natural full-parameter volume-fraction question. This is not merely an arbitrary single instance or recomputation from a known value.
